draft.title: Best buys with unit prices
card: Products come in different sizes, so the shelf prices cannot be compared directly. A unit price is the cost for one fixed amount, such as cents per 100 g.
To find a unit price, divide the price by how many units are in the pack. Change dollars to cents first if you want cents.
Worked example: a 250 g jar costs $3.00, which is 300 cents. There are 2.5 lots of 100 g, so \(300 \div 2.5 = 120\) cents per 100 g.
Work out the unit price of each product using the same unit. The best buy is the one with the lowest unit price.
draft.remember: Use the same unit for every product, then pick the lowest unit price.

a.q: Pack A has 500 g of rice for $2.00. Pack B has 200 g for $1.00. Which is the best buy, and why?
opts: Pack A, at 40 cents per 100 g
Pack B, at 50 cents per 100 g
Pack A, at 50 cents per 100 g
Pack B, at 40 cents per 100 g
a.why: Pack A is 200 cents for 5 lots of 100 g, which is 40 cents per 100 g. Pack B is 100 cents for 2 lots, which is 50 cents per 100 g. The lower unit price is the best buy, so Pack A wins even though it costs more in total.
a.clue: Find the cents for each 100 g in both packs.

b.q: Juice at Tom's shop: 2 L for $3.60, 1.5 L for $2.85 and 750 mL for $1.50. Which is the best buy?
opts: All have the same unit price
b.why: Per litre the prices are $1.80, $1.90 and $2.00. The 2 L bottle has the lowest unit price. The 750 mL bottle has the lowest shelf price, but that does not make it the best buy.
b.clue: Work out the cost of 1 L for each bottle. Change 750 mL to litres first.

a.best: Pack A, at 40 cents per 100 g
